summary: Dashboard series facet ordering appears randomized after live refresh, breaking drilldowns
description:
Issue summary:
When viewing a dashboard with a high-cardinality 'series' facet, users report that the ordering of the series list becomes effectively randomized each time the live panel refreshes. This causes the drilldown links for popular series to change position and, in some cases, the exported drilldown link points to the wrong series.

Impact:
- OrbitAnalytics (dedicated customer) reports recurring user-facing confusion and incorrect drilldowns on three production dashboards used by their analysts.
- Analysts rely on stable facet ordering to validate alerts and run ad-hoc investigations; incorrect drilldowns lead to wasted time and occasional incorrect conclusions.
- Reproducible for the customer on multiple browsers and appears to affect dashboards with >500 unique series in the time window.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (hosted) serving OrbitAnalytics dedicated org
- Region: us-east
- Dashboards: traffic-anomalies-weekly, model-inference-attribution
- Time window: last 7 days, auto-refresh enabled (30s)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login as OrbitAnalytics user and open 'traffic-anomalies-weekly' dashboard.
2) Expand series facet in the left rail and observe top N series ordering.
3) Toggle auto-refresh on (30s) and let it run 2-3 cycles.
4) Observe position changes in the series list.
5) Click drilldown on a top series immediately after a refresh; the drilldown sometimes navigates to a different series than the label clicked.

Observed behavior:
- Facet list order changes on each refresh for customers with high-cardinality series (>=500).
- Drilldown links sometimes carry an index-based param (series_index=42) that no longer matches the label at that index after reordering.

Expected behavior:
- Series facet ordering should be stable between refreshes (consistent sort key) and drilldown links should resolve to the label the user clicked regardless of reordering or refresh timing.

Temporary workaround:
- Customer disabled auto-refresh and uses manual refresh when needed; this limits but does not eliminate the issue because other users occasionally trigger re-render flows.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Reproduced in prod with OrbitAnalytics account. Frontend shows non-deterministic ordering after refresh cycles on dashboards with >500 series.

2026-03-11: Hypothesis: client-side facet rendering relies on iteration order of a JS Set/Object created from backend map; when backend emits series in streaming chunks the client appends without a stable sort. Also found index-based drilldown parameter creation that assumes stable ordering.

2026-03-11: Backend confirmed that series payload arrives in streaming batches; no explicit sort key is enforced by the server for high-cardinality response to avoid extra compute. See Slack: #support thread <#support/console-ops> (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C04SUP12345).

2026-03-11: Frontend prototype: enforced sort by 'count desc, label asc' eliminates reordering in local repro. Created PR to add deterministic sort and switch drilldown to use series_id instead of series_index.

2026-03-12: Confirmed that switching drilldown to series_id addresses incorrect navigation even if ordering changes. Patch prepared in frontend (PR 4829) and a companion backend change to include stable series_id in the streaming payload is required.

Related artifacts: related_github_prs and confluence debugging page added to ticket. Linked to SUP-61234 which has a separate saved-query timeout that surfaced during reproductions; also cross-referenced SUP-781409 which previously dealt with missing trace links after retention operations.
comments:
2026-03-10 - OrbitAnalytics (Samir Patel): 'We're seeing top items jump around every 30s; it's causing our alert audits to point to the wrong service. Can you advise?
Attached screenshots and a short Loom.

2026-03-10 - Support (Avery Chen): 'Thanks Samir — we've triaged and can reproduce on your org. We're escalating to frontend and putting the dashboard into read-only for a short window if we need to test changes. ETA initial findings 24h.'

2026-03-11 - Frontend Eng (Riley Moore): 'Found that client is not applying a deterministic sort when merging streaming batches. Working on a patch to sort by count desc + label asc and to switch drilldown payload to use series_id. Will post PR.'

2026-03-12 - Support (Avery Chen): 'Applied temporary mitigation: disabled client-side population of index-based drilldown for the OrbitAnalytics org. This prevents incorrect navigation for now while we roll the fix. Please verify on your side.'

2026-03-12 - OrbitAnalytics (Samir Patel): 'Confirmed that drilldowns now point to the correct series. Ordering still visually moves but drilldown correctness is acceptable for our workflow. Thanks — please advise when full fix lands.'
resolution: Mitigation applied: client-side index-based drilldown generation disabled for affected org while fix rolls out. Hotfix PR submitted to console-ui to enforce stable sorting and to change drilldown to use series_id; backend change to include series_id in streaming payload opened. Next steps: roll frontend hotfix through staging, run e2e with high-cardinality fixture, and deploy to prod. Post-deploy follow-up: add unit tests for streaming merge + deterministic sort and add dashboard e2e for drilldown correctness. Owner: Riley Moore.
